create.title: Hard-TOP t=1 residual K17a primitive alias conductor reduction
create.statement_tex: Within the accepted low-cross-gcd complement kappa_*<delta L of the exact two-orientation K17a identity, write g=(u,n), u=g u_0, n=g n_0, and (n_0,u_0)=1. The primitive anchor satisfies E_u(+/- vbar n)=E_(u_0)(+/- vbar n_0), and its normalized Fourier aliases fold exactly as sum_(j=0)^(g-1)c_u(ell+j u_0)=c_(u_0)(ell). For q=u_0/(ell,u_0), ell=(u_0/q)a, and (a,q)=1, one has c_(u_0)(ell)=(q/u_0)c_q(a) and sum_(cond(ell)=q)|c_(u_0)(ell)|<<(q/u_0)log(2q). A fixed (kappa,u,u_0) stratum has O(u_0 L) literal atoms, so its exact-q positive capacity is O(L q log(2q)). Consequently, for every fixed B>0 and Q_B=(log(2X))^B, the complete exact Fourier packet q<=Q_B is <<_(B,delta,gamma,epsilon)L^2 X^epsilon. This packet contains the complete physical sector u/(u,n)<=Q_B; its exact Fourier complement is q>Q_B. Exact rank-one alias TT* reconstructs the physical block, while alias Parseval, positive bucket closure, one-conductor-square-root recombination, lift-erasing completion, and complementary-divisor orientation pairing give only the scoped capacity or self-return limitations recorded in the kernel and no literal lower mass. The sufficient high-q estimates (177.K34)--(177.K35), complete K17a, every parent, and every exponent implication remain open.
